candidates.source: landscape-sweep-20260926: Layer alternatives list (conditional), plus the open-gap analysis, a GitHub GraphQL/REST changelog read and the official Claude Code/Agent SDK docs
candidates.demonstrated_gap: Open gap 5 (independent-host recovery and power-loss durability unqualified) has no built-in native answer on the Claude side. The official sessions doc says session files stay on the machine that created them and plain resume works on that machine only. The first-party Python SDK adds an operator-owned SessionStore (0.1.64, with a 13-contract conformance harness and reference S3/Redis/Postgres adapters). Its session_store_flush='eager' option is documented for cross-process resume and crash durability (0.1.73), and it adds resume_drops_turn/resume_session_at guards (0.2.137), in-process @tool MCP servers and hook callbacks. It still runs the unmodified bundled Claude Code (0.2.160 bundles CLI 2.1.283). Anthropic's legal page lets an end user sign in to the unmodified binary with their own subscription, and the help center describes Agent SDK use on Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise plan credentials, so the same-account check is feasible. The same trial also yields the first macos-arm64 evidence; both winners are untested there.
candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: Use one frozen bounded research task with the same native claude login (no API key), model and effort on the WSL workstation and a Mac. Arm A (native): claude -p --output-format stream-json --session-id on WSL, SIGKILL mid-tool-call, copy the JSONL to the Mac and run claude --resume there. Arm B (SDK 0.2.160): the same task with a self-hosted reference Redis or Postgres SessionStore on the workstation (passing run_session_store_conformance), session_store_flush='eager', SIGKILL mid-turn, then resume from the store on the Mac with the same cwd. Adopt B only if it matches A on account identity and plan-usage attribution, exactly-once external effects, transcript completeness up to the kill and cache-read/token totals, and loses less state at the kill point. Keep native if copying the file recovers the same state, or if B needs an API key or any other non-native credential.

candidates.source: landscape-sweep-20260926: The ACP registry protocol matrix and the goose ACP-provider docs, found by following codex-acp (a catalogued conditional component); verified with GitHub GraphQL/REST
candidates.demonstrated_gap: This layer has no gap for it today. It is the Claude counterpart to codex-acp, which is already conditional for ACP hosts such as DeerFlow. It runs the unmodified Claude Code through the Agent SDK over ACP, and was renamed from zed-industries/claude-code-acp. The ACP registry probe of 2026-09-25 shows claude-acp 0.81.2 advertising loadSession, session/list, session/fork and session/resume, the same set as codex-acp 1.13.1. It also adds an opt-in sessionFailure extension: durable, revisioned error and warning records with a category (connection/access/limit/...) and recommended recovery actions. It adds compaction and permission extensions as well, which gives structured recovery events that the plain stream-json path does not name. It releases often (v0.78.0 to v0.81.2 between 2026-09-15 and 2026-09-24). It matters only if an ACP host must drive both native clients through one protocol.
candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: In one ACP host, run the frozen research prompt through claude-acp 0.81.x and codex-acp 1.13.x, and compare against native claude -p and codex exec. Kill the adapter mid-turn, then call session/resume. Score event completeness (tool calls, usage, sessionFailure category and actions), account identity (sign-in completed through Anthropic's own flow), exactly-once effects and tokens. Promote it only when an ACP-host requirement exists and claude-acp matches the native path on every check.

candidates.source: landscape-sweep-20260926: Follow-up critic seed (skill-scanner 2.1.0 for the deferred skill-security slot). Source reviewed read-only through GitHub GraphQL and code search; scoped supply-chain-risk-auditor run on its LLM and rule-engine dependencies.
candidates.demonstrated_gap:
The skill-security slot is deferred because both reviewed scanners read through an outside symlink on the m7 fixture. superagent-ai skill-security printed the canary. getsentry skill-scanner flagged the link as critical but still read the file behind it.

Source read of Cisco skill-scanner (HEAD 4f8bec34; release 2.1.0, 2026-09-05):
- The default loader skips symlinks during file discovery (loader.py l.429).
- It resolves every discovered file through realpath plus a root-prefix check before reading (loader.py l.432; file_utils.py resolve_path_within_root l.41; read_text_strict with root l.84-100).
- Upstream carries a path-containment test, tests/test_codeql_path_security.py.
- The core engines run without any API key: YAML and YARA-X signatures, bytecode, pipeline and behavioral dataflow. The LLM, meta, VirusTotal and AI Defense stages are opt-in.

Residual paths the source does not close:
- strict_structure.py calls read_text_strict(skill_md_path) with no root.
- adjudicator.py and meta_analyzer.py call Path.read_text directly.
- So a SKILL.md that is itself an outside symlink, or an opt-in analyzer, may still read outside the skill.

Other weaknesses:
- Upstream's own source-disjoint benchmark is weak: precision 60.75%, recall 7.75%, F1 13.74%, and it fails upstream's promotion gate. The dev split reports precision 99.16% and recall 31.43%.
- litellm>=1.84.0, anthropic and openai are mandatory dependencies.
candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: Install 2.1.0 in an isolated uv tool environment with network denied. Run the default scan and the --use-behavioral scan on m7, and on an m7 variant whose SKILL.md is the outside symlink, under an open()/openat trace. Any open of the outside canary, or its marker in the output, rejects it on the same grounds as the other two scanners. Then compare on the 7 synthetic malicious fixtures (skill-security 6/7, getsentry skill-scanner 4/7 at high or critical) and count false positives on the 28 pinned trial skills. Adopt for the slot only with zero outside opens, at least 6/7 detection and no more false positives than skill-security.

candidates.demonstrated_gap: The #274 R1 rerun has no zero-install native arm, yet Codex ships a Stable local memory. At rust-v0.157.1 `features.memories` is Stage::Stable with default_enabled false. It stores plain files under CODEX_HOME (v2 in a separate memories_v2 store with its own SQLite DB). Other controls: per-thread memory modes, a filter that keeps MCP and web-search threads out of generation, and secret-redacting consolidation. Forget and correction requests become ad hoc notes applied at consolidation. User edits are diffed against a git baseline, and deleted content is not kept in the prompt artifact or in unreachable git objects. A full reset clears both versions, and thread deletion removes that thread from both stores. An UnderDevelopment one-way import copies Claude-layout project memory into Codex; it is the only native cross-client path. A third-party memory owner has to beat this arm on quality and complete usage to justify a second owner in Codex. Limits to measure rather than assume: the summary is global to the user, with project scope only as headings. Dedicated search is unranked lexical line matching capped at 200 hits, and the tools are off unless dedicated_tools=true. Generation runs only when a root session starts, on rollouts idle at least min_rollout_idle_hours (default 6, range 1-48), two rollouts per startup by default. Subagent and ephemeral sessions are never captured. Extraction and consolidation use plan quota and are skipped below 25% remaining rate limit.
candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: Add these arms to the #274 R1 rerun: a no-memory control (features.memories=false), a full-context control (the roughly 115k-token LongMemEval-S history in context) and Codex memories v2. Run Codex in a disposable CODEX_HOME with its own native sign-in (never copied credentials), set memories=true, version=v2, dedicated_tools=true, min_rollout_idle_hours=1 and max_rollouts_per_startup=128, and schedule it outside running workflows. Give every arm the same preregistered real sessions. These combine a stratified LongMemEval-S slice replayed from the oracle evidence sessions, including abstention items (recall_all@5 skips the 30 abstention instances), with a project corpus of decisions, handoffs, corrections and forget requests. Score blind end-to-end accuracy, abstention accuracy, forgetting after ad hoc forget notes, thread deletion and reset, and complete provider usage including the extract and consolidation passes. If Codex memories sit inside the paired CI of agentmemory D2 and ai-memory C3'/C4' and beat the no-memory control at equal or lower complete usage, a third-party owner is not justified for Codex-only recall. If they trail D2 by a margin whose CI excludes zero, they stay the native control only.

candidates.demonstrated_gap: The adopted pipeline has no accelerator series at all. origin/main (20b52a5b) has zero references to dcgm, nvidia_gpu_exporter, macmon, mactop, all-smi, windows_exporter or process-exporter. The adopted Collector's host_metrics receiver scrapes only cpu, memory, load and filesystem, and collector-contrib has no GPU or NVIDIA receiver at HEAD. The 2026-09-26 local-inference plan admits and guards arms on whole-device memory.free from ad-hoc 1 Hz nvidia-smi shell samples that stay outside the pipeline (plan.json L18, L449, L482). vLLM's /metrics is engine-level only. So VRAM, power, temperature and clock history cannot be reconciled with engine and native counters in the one privacy-filtered pipeline. This exporter targets GeForce-class GPUs and reads the same nvidia-smi the plan already calls (/usr/lib/wsl/lib/nvidia-smi). It also has an experimental NVML backend on Linux. It bounds collection with --collect.timeout and a background mode, and it reports failed collections explicitly. Since v1.15.0 it ships cosign-signed checksums, signed tags and build-provenance attestations. Scope correction from read-only local probes on this workstation (driver 616.64, RTX 4090): inside WSL, device-level utilization, power, temperature, SM clock and memory all answer and match the Windows-side WDDM view. Per-process memory is N/A on both sides. So a Windows-host deployment adds nothing here, and the trial belongs inside WSL.

Adopt only if all of these hold: (a) paired memory.free/used values agree within 1 MiB for at least 99% of pairs; (b) failed collections appear as a failure series, not as healthy-looking gaps; (c) under a known load, utilization.gpu stays within 5 percentage points of Windows-side nvidia-smi.exe read through interop; (d) the exporter's background nvidia-smi polling does not raise window.sh query latency or cause guard timeouts; (e) at least one cross-signal query works that the ad-hoc files cannot answer, such as vLLM kv_cache_usage_perc against device memory.used. Overturn if values disagree, if it only duplicates window.sh capture, or if WSL utilization diverges under load, which would confirm NVIDIA's documented limitation for that field. Test the NVML backend separately; if it fails under WSL where the nvidia-smi backend works, keep the nvidia-smi backend.

candidates.source: landscape-sweep-20260926: Seeded by the completeness critic (follow-up round). Verified with GitHub GraphQL: release notes for v1.6.0/v1.6.3 and v1.6.3 source files (predictor, ValidationStructure, _setup_utils, timeseries models), plus a GitHub Advisory Database query.
candidates.demonstrated_gap: The retained broad-universe study (4,577,640 scored decisions, 45,406,248 events, 71 s) tested 5 predeclared signals x 3 horizons one at a time, and all 15 cells came back not_established. No multi-signal learned model has been run under that frozen chronology, and neither winner provides one: skfolio covers portfolio optimisation and WalkForward, EdgarTools covers filings. LightGBM survived the 2026-09-23 sweep only as a single learner. AutoGluon 1.6.x is a maintained reference AutoML baseline. 1.6.0 added `validation_structure` (time_on/group_time_on, temporal_forward_only), so internal splits respect time order. It added an `extreme` preset whose release notes say every model in it is free for commercial use; TabPFN-3 is confined to a separate `noncommercial` preset. It also exposes Chronos2Model and Toto2Model in TimeSeriesPredictor, which gives one harness for the forecasting comparison below. Two limits were verified in v1.6.3 source. First, ValidationStructure has no purge, embargo or gap parameter, and its default temporal mode is leave-one-block-out, so folds train on later blocks. Internal validation therefore cannot be trusted with overlapping H5/H20 labels, and outer splits must be external. Second, core/_setup_utils.py caps pandas <2.4.0 and pyarrow <25.0.0, while the repository pins pandas 3.0.6 and pyarrow 25.0.1, so AutoGluon needs its own environment. Governance changed in 1.6.0: maintainers now span Amazon and Prior Labs, the maker of TabPFN.
candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: Offline run with no refetch, in an isolated venv (Python 3.13, pandas 2.3.x, extreme preset only, never noncommercial). Fit TabularPredictor on the frozen broad-universe feature panel inside the same skfolio WalkForward outer folds, with purged_size at least the label horizon (20 sessions for H20) plus an embargo. Use either num_bag_folds=0 with an explicit tuning_data block that ends before the purge, or validation_structure={'time_on': <date>, 'temporal_forward_only': True} with stacking off. Score out-of-sample rank IC and cost-adjusted top-minus-bottom decile returns per horizon against a default LightGBM and a ridge baseline on identical folds, with a date-clustered block bootstrap. Add a label-permutation placebo, whose IC must be indistinguishable from zero, and a deliberately injected one-session look-ahead feature, which the chronology audit must flag. Adopt only if AutoGluon beats LightGBM by a preregistered margin with the CI excluding zero and passes both canaries on linux-wsl2. No margin, or any canary failure, relabels it not_adopted, and LightGBM stays the learned baseline.

candidates.demonstrated_gap: Open gap 2 says the 6-row purge plus interval assertions 'does not establish independent samples' for overlapping 5-session labels. Gap 3 says the chronology and inference logic lives in project-local wrappers. The broad-universe study (15 signal x horizon cells) relies on local date-clustered block-bootstrap Bonferroni intervals, and its README says 'the Bonferroni bound from 2,000 resamples is noisy'. Neither winner does factor inference: a GitHub code search of skfolio for 'deflated' returns 0 hits, and the listed alphalens-reloaded alternative has had no push since 2025-12-15. factrix is upstream, Polars-native and Apache-2.0. Its dependencies are polars>=1.38.1,<2 (compatible with the stack's polars 1.44.2 pin), numpy and scipy. It requires Python >=3.12, which the research venv's 3.13.15 meets. Its test suite at 233b29d covers overlap-aware HAC predictive_beta (Amihud-Hurvich with Bartlett overlap bandwidth), Driscoll-Kraay pooled beta, Fama-MacBeth betas, Stambaugh bias, hierarchical and cross-metric BHY FDR, event-study CAAR, Corrado rank tests and event-overlap discipline. Together these are the missing inference layer for the ETF control lane and the catalyst event direction. Risks: one active committer, 10 stars, pre-1.0 with 26 PyPI releases since 2026-05-07, and no detailed changelog. Pin to v0.33.0 / 233b29d.

candidates.demonstrated_gap: Unattended IBKR paper-gateway operation now depends on a retired component, and nothing has been selected to replace it. On develop, NautilusTrader's DockerizedIBGateway uses ghcr.io/gnzsnz/ib-gateway:stable by default. That image's stable Dockerfile installs IBC 3.24.2 on Gateway 10.50.1e. IBC was retired on 2026-09-01 and its repository is archived. gnzsnz#366 has been open since 2026-03-24 and no replacement has been chosen. ibg-controller is a maintained, MIT-licensed replacement. It keeps the gnzsnz environment contract (TWS_USERID, TRADING_MODE, TWOFA_DEVICE) and IBC's command-server names, and it drives Gateway from an agent inside the JVM. It adds several things IBC lacks: it takes over Gateway's own daily restart without starting a second JVM or logging in again; it logs out cleanly on stop so session slots are not stranded; it halts by default on a persistent CCP lockout; it has a structured ALERT_* log contract and *_FILE secret inputs; and it publishes multi-arch images signed with cosign (keyless) with a syft SPDX SBOM, built by SHA-pinned actions. The trial must cover these limits. Login, 2FA and dialog handling are verified only on Gateway 10.45.x; its ci.yml says nothing is verified on 10.50, which is the current gnzsnz stable line. Its release images pin 10.45.1j. Unattended 2FA needs a Mobile Authenticator TOTP seed, which is a new stored credential. IB Key push still needs a person. TWS mode is written but not run. One maintainer (30 stars, 8 forks).
candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: On the workstation with the IBKR paper login, run the same frozen gateway-lifecycle suite for at least 7 consecutive days, including one Sunday 01:00 ET re-authentication. Measure: cold-start login success; daily restarts that need no re-authentication; time until Nautilus DockerizedIBGateway sees the API as ready; recovery after a forced socket drop and after docker stop (session slots released); whether the Gateway meets the protocol-213 minimum that Nautilus PR #5041 enforces; whether any secret appears in docker logs (the TOTP seed must never be printed, see gnzsnz#443); and attended minutes per week. Adopt B only if it matches or beats A on every case, passes on the 10.50 line and leaks no secret. If C gives the paper lane the same unattended hours, keep the native path and add no controller. Reopen if gnzsnz#366 adopts a different integrated replacement or ibg-controller loses its maintainer.

The documented path for MLflow (c1) is `mlflow autolog claude`, which writes hooks into .claude/settings.json before a session starts. Scout 0.5.3 comes from the Inspect maintainers (MIT, 1,770 commits, 33 mentionable users, released 2026-09-23). A trial can therefore run offline, with zero provider calls and no new credentials, on both hosts. The transcript database stays private and only sanitized counts are kept. Source review and GitHub metadata only: no candidate was installed, run, benchmarked or compared with a winner; survival means the proposal withstood fact and fit checks, not that it beats a winner.

Harness: this run used the 2026-09-26 scratchpad prototype of the lane, not the packaged tools/sota-convergence/landscape-sweep/ harness merged afterwards (#324). Layer inputs: the prototype's input builder cut known-repository slugs with rstrip('.git'). A local check against the GitHub repositories named in this repository's catalogs and manifests finds 95 of the 614 known-repository slugs cut, in 30 of the 32 layers (qdrant/qdrant appeared as qdrant/qdran, pydantic/pydantic-ai as pydantic/pydantic-a), so discovery saw slightly wrong known-repository lists. The ledger's known/new split is recomputed from the manifest baseline and is not affected.

GPT-6 lanes: 16 of the 80 GPT-6 jobs returned nothing; evidence/artifacts/landscape-sweep-20260926/gpt6-jobs.json keeps each job's times and markers. Two discovery jobs ended with the shared Codex account's usage-limit error event (03:47-03:55Z), and six jobs (five discovery, one fit) were refused by the runner's usage-limit marker from 03:57Z to 04:12Z; the coordinator records the account signed in again at 04:15Z. Eight first-round fit jobs requested from 04:17Z to 05:35Z never started: the prototype runner's start command split its shell script at an embedded quote in its usage-limit event check (added at about 03:57Z, per the coordinator's incident log), which shifted its arguments, so its slot loop never obtained a slot; the next fit job started at 05:52Z. The seven layers without a GPT-6 discovery return have Claude-only discovery. In the nine layers without GPT-6 first-round fit votes a missing vote counts as refuted: those proposals are not survivors, their only fit votes are Claude's, and they are never counted as two-family agreement. Every affected layer is reopened (retained_failure). The false usage-limit marker of 02:17Z (text in a cited README matched the prototype's check) fell in the stopped run 1, not in this run.

Seeds: the run's seeds (tools/sota-convergence/landscape-sweep/seeds-20260926.json) placed two candidates differently from manifests/candidates.json: NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM under observation-inference (candidates.json: semantic-rag), and EleutherAI/lm-evaluation-harness under quality-evaluation only (candidates.json: also us-equities evaluation-experiments). Call counts cover discovery only (both families, as each worker reported them); refuter and critic calls are not counted. counts.trading_layers_note: trading_layers counts only taxonomy layers with at least one selected entry, unlike foundation_layers (which counts every row); trading[] itself always has one row per taxonomy id, so len(manifest["trading"]) can exceed trading_layers whenever a taxonomy layer happens to have zero selected entries
counts.pin_status_note: pins_behind_upstream counts the generator's computed pin fields; pins_behind_upstream_by_review_status splits those rows by published review_status. A row's review_status is pin_behind_upstream[_unverified] only when its computed pin_behind_upstream is true, so review_status_pin_behind_upstream equals the pin_behind_upstream[_unverified] share of that split; a lane pin claim the computed fields contradict is published as pin_status_disputed[_unverified] (the lane's claim in disputed_lane_status and the row evidence) or, on an OS-package pin, distro_managed
counts.pins_behind_note: components with a commit-pinned version (a parenthetical hash), a non-GitHub repository, or an OS-distribution package pin (matched by an -Nubuntu/-Ndeb/+debN pin suffix, or by id via --os-package-ids, e.g. systemd even though its own repository is on GitHub) are excluded from the pin-vs-upstream comparison rather than counted either way
counts.pins_not_compared_note: rows whose pin the generator could not compare with upstream (the exclusions above, plus a pin or upstream latest with no parseable version, reason unversioned) carry pin_behind_upstream null and pin_comparison not_compared, never a definite false
counts.lane_groupings_note: every foundation/trading-scoped count above (candidates_total, candidates_by_disposition, components_confirmed, pins_behind_upstream, pins_behind_upstream_unique_components) is computed from all_rows = manifest['foundation'] + manifest['trading'] only, and so excludes lane_groupings[].selected rows the same way it excludes lane_groupings[].candidates; candidates inside lane_groupings (a review-lane grouping id outside the foundation/taxonomy baseline, e.g. an awesome-list survey) are counted only in lane_grouping_candidates; counts.citation_review (computed below, by apply_citation_review) is the same way scoped -- its rows_flagged/attached only ever count a foundation/trading row, never a lane_groupings[].selected row, since apply_citation_review only walks manifest['foundation'] and manifest['trading']
